Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards
Situation2: An external inspector has raised immediate concerns that could halt operations unless issues are resolved
Story: My phone buzzed violently just as I was reviewing the inspector’s urgent email. The subject line—“Immediate Safety Compliance Required”—made my stomach clench. I knew the plant couldn’t afford a shutdown, and as the lead engineer, it was my responsibility to address the inspector’s concerns before morning. I was already drafting a plan when my phone rang again, this time with my friend’s name flashing on the screen. Her voice was shaky, almost in tears—her car had broken down on the highway, and she was alone, scared, and needed me to pick her up right away. I could hear trucks roaring past her in the background. My mind raced: my friend was counting on me to be there, but so was my team, and the company’s operations depended on my immediate action. I felt torn in two, the weight of both expectations pressing down on me, my heart pounding as I stared at the two urgent demands, knowing I couldn’t possibly meet them both at once.
